elements.name: intro_body
elements.text:
Reliable optical inspection requires clear boundaries and stable feature positions. R152 reconstructs microscopy images on the original pixel grid and connects them to one geometric measurement pipeline.

One fixed set of learned weights processes 20× and 50× images with objective-specific optical information. Bounded correction preserves the input geometry while sharpening the measured boundaries [1, 2].

elements.name: methods_body
elements.text:
R152 combines PSF-guided reconstruction, anti-aliased processing and bounded output correction. The optical inputs comprise 25 kernels at 20× and one calibrated kernel at 50×.

All image methods share one LSC pipeline [3, 4]. Each pillar uses 720 radial samples and three center-refinement passes. The median horizontal shift of nine pillars defines each step.

elements.name: conclusions_body
elements.text:
R152 reduces median within-grid variation from 10.86 nm to 4.26 nm, a 60.8% reduction relative to Raw.

Step SD and nominal MAE decrease by 19.5% and 23.1%, respectively. The same learned weights deliver the lowest measured values in every tested condition.

Step variation reaches 0.056 pixel at 20× and 0.067 pixel at 50×. R152 combines clear pillar boundaries with stronger positional consistency across both objectives.
